bugs: app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:91-100 marks the import Completed before sending the email synchronously. If Mail::send throws, the retry hits the claim guard at line 35 (status is no longer queued/processing), returns early, and the summary email is never sent.

app/Imports/ProductRowParser.php:30 stock has no upper bound. A value like 99999999999 passes validation and is upserted into an unsignedInteger column. On MySQL that fails the whole chunk's upsert and the job, instead of recording one row error.
Retrying a partially processed import (status still processing) counts products upserted on the first attempt as 'updated' rather than 'created', so the counts drift.
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:17 abort_if($path === false, 503) is ceremony; store() failures normally throw.
app/Imports/ProductRowParser.php:24-32 hand-written match(true) validation instead of the Validator / validation rules the framework already provides.
app/Imports/ProductRowParser.php:13 returns array{error}|array{product} shapes instead of a small DTO or exception, and the job checks isset($result['error']).
app/Models/Import.php:20 the $attributes default uses the string 'queued' instead of ImportStatus::Queued->value.
tests/Feature/ImportTest.php:232 calls handle() with FQCNs inline instead of imports.
strengths: Proper API setup: routes/api.php registered in bootstrap/app.php, Sanctum auth:sanctum, and a guest redirect returning null for api/* so non-JSON guests get 401.
Authorization on the route via ->can('view','import') with an ImportPolicy that uses relation->is().
Bulk upsert per 500-row chunk with LazyCollection streaming, which scales to 5MB files; duplicate SKUs within a chunk are deduplicated.
Atomic status claim (conditional update) prevents double processing; the job uses Tries/Backoff/Timeout/DeleteWhenMissingModels attributes.
Handles BOM, header case, blank lines and ragged rows; a missing header fails the import with a recorded reason.
Uses File::types()->max() fluent rule, returns 202 Accepted, and the resource uses whenLoaded.
Thorough tests: exact 5MB boundary, chunk-spanning file, idempotent rerun, header failure, mail content assertions.

bugs: routes/web.php:10-13 puts the API endpoints in web.php under an 'api' prefix with session 'auth'. CSRF/forgery protection therefore applies, and a probe with the unit-test bypass disabled returned 419 on POST /api/imports. Real API clients cannot upload.
routes/web.php:10 a non-JSON guest request to GET /api/imports/{id} returns 500 (the login route is not defined) instead of 401; confirmed by probe.
tests/Feature/ImportTest.php:80-88 'accepts file of exactly 5mb' actually asserts 422 (the fake file has no header), so the 5MB boundary acceptance is never tested.
Retrying a partially processed import counts products created on the first attempt as 'updated'.
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:42-69 a missing file makes readStream return null, so the error is a TypeError from fgetcsv/fclose(null) rather than a clear exception.
antipatterns: routes/web.php:10 API routes defined in web.php instead of installing api routes plus a token guard (Sanctum).
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:60,127 one query per error row plus updateOrCreate per valid row (2+ queries per row); a 5MB file means hundreds of thousands of queries, where upsert in chunks would do.
app/Jobs/ProcessImport.php:109 builds a Validator per row: idiomatic, but expensive inside a hot loop.
app/Http/Resources/ImportResource.php:26 accesses $this->rowErrors unconditionally instead of whenLoaded, so it risks lazy loading.
app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:24 eager-loads rowErrors on a freshly created import, a wasted query.
Column list duplicated in StoreImportRequest::REQUIRED_COLUMNS and ProcessImport::COLUMNS, and the BOM/header normalisation is duplicated too.
app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:29 Gate::authorize in the controller where route ->can() middleware would do.
strengths: The header columns are validated up front in the FormRequest after() hook, so bad files are rejected with 422 before an Import is created.
Uses Laravel's Validator for row rules, giving standard messages and min/max/integer bounds including the stock upper limit.
A queued Notification (ShouldQueue) for the summary email decouples mail failures from the import job.
Intention-revealing model methods markProcessing/markCompleted/markFailed; supports reordered columns via header mapping.
Tests cover a crash-retry clearing stale errors, a header-only file, an exact JSON structure, and the guest/other-user/404 paths.

v.rationale: Both suites pass (impl-1: 20 tests, impl-2: 24). They differ on correctness and architecture. impl-1 sets up a real API: api.php, Sanctum token auth, route-level ->can() authorization and a 202 response. Processing streams the file and upserts in 500-row chunks with an atomic status claim. My probes confirmed it handles header-only and empty files, ragged rows, quoted commas and a missing header. Its weaknesses are smaller: if the synchronous email fails, it is lost on retry; stock has no upper bound; and validation is hand-written instead of using Laravel's Validator. impl-2 has nicer pieces: header validation in the FormRequest, a per-row Validator and a queued Notification. But it registers the 'API' in web.php with session auth. With the test bypass disabled, a probe got 419 on POST /api/imports, and a non-JSON guest request returned 500. Its exact-5MB test also does not test what its name says, and processing costs at least two queries per row. impl-2's routing bug means real API clients cannot use the main endpoint, so impl-1 ranks first.
